_comment: NeoForge composites this bucket at runtime from an empty bucket and a tinted fluid mask (its
'neoforge:fluid_container' item model), which is why the NeoForge tree needs no bucket texture.
Fabric has no equivalent, so the same composite is spelled out as two layers here.
layer0 is vanilla's EMPTY bucket, so the metal keeps vanilla's own shading. layer1 is a greyscale
mask of just the liquid surface, which the client item tints to the fluid's colour -- tint index 1,
because a generated item model gives each layer the tint index of its own number. Tinting is a
multiply, which is why the mask is greyscale and why vanilla's water_bucket sprite cannot be used
directly: its blue is baked in and no tint turns blue into green. This is the same arrangement the
fluid itself uses in the world -- vanilla's greyscale block/water_still, tinted.
